issue_title: EventDispatcher.close() releases a mutex held by a publishing thread
issue_body:

## Minimally Reproducible Test Case Run this from a checkout of Celery `main`:

```python from threading import Event, Thread from celery import Celery app = Celery("dispatcher_close_race", broker="memory://") publish_started = Event() finish_publish = Event() close_started = Event() close_finished = Event() errors = [] with app.connection_for_write() as connection: dispatcher = app.events.Dispatcher( connection, buffer_while_offline=False ) actual_publish = dispatcher.producer.publish def blocking_publish(*args, **kwargs): publish_started.set() if not finish_publish.wait(5): raise TimeoutError("publish was not allowed to finish") return actual_publish(*args, **kwargs) dispatcher.producer.publish = blocking_publish def send(): try: dispatcher.send("task-sent") except Exception as exc: errors.append(f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}") def close(): close_started.set() try: dispatcher.close() finally: close_finished.set() publisher = Thread(target=send) closer = Thread(target=close) publisher.start() assert publish_started.wait(5) try: closer.start() assert close_started.wait(5) closed_before_publish = close_finished.wait(0.2) finally: finish_publish.set() publisher.join(5) closer.join(5) assert not publisher.is_alive() and not closer.is_alive() print("close returned before publish finished:", closed_before_publish) print("publisher errors:", errors) ```

On `main`, this prints: ```text close returned before publish finished: True publisher errors: ['RuntimeError: release unlocked lock'] ``` ## Expected Behavior `close()` should wait for an in-flight event publication to leave the dispatcher’s critical section. The publishing thread should finish without a lock error; only then should `close()` clear the producer and return. ## Actual Behavior [`EventDispatcher.close()` on `main`](https://github.com/celery/celery/blob/57cfb4629bbf919e24ff85f33d1eca038c973f4d/celery/events/dispatcher.py#L224-L229) calls `self.mutex.release()` whenever the primitive lock is locked, even when another thread owns the ongoing publication. `close()` returns and clears `producer` while that publication is still in progress. When the publishing thread exits `with self.mutex:`, it raises: ```text Traceback (most recent call last): File "", line 24, in send File "upstream/main:celery/events/dispatcher.py", line 197, in send return self.publish(type, fields, self.producer, blind=blind, ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "upstream/main:celery/events/dispatcher.py", line 138, in publish with self.mutex: RuntimeError: release unlocked lock ``` The interleaving was reproduced using the dispatcher source from `main` at the commit identified above.
